discoveries: The kernel schema (`path-map.schema.json`) requires nine fields per namespace, but the loader on `w2/integrate` checks all nine only when a map has all four W1-08 keys (state_class, capabilities, policies, systems). These planted maps have at most one, so the loader's minimal check applies: `paths`, if present, must be a non-empty list. `{all: {paths: ['**']}}` is the least it accepts, and core-pathmap reports no finding on it (all cases green). `**` has to be quoted in YAML flow style (a bare `*` starts an alias). The whole W1-30 suite takes longer than 540 s at `-n 8` here; the batches took about 21 minutes in all.
risks: The planted maps don't meet the full kernel schema; they never did, and they are only judged by the loader's minimal mode. If the loader later requires the full namespace fields of every map, these planted maps would need the seven CAP-03.c fields.
lessons: Run W1-30 in by-file batches from the start: one command does not finish in 540 s. Scratch cleanup with `rm -rf` in the session temp folder was refused for permission, so plan cleanup for a mode where it is allowed.
